model.name: Risk / Control
model.purpose: Attach risk and control assurance context to a host subject: project relevant risk statements, link them to referenced controls with an explicit claimed treatment mechanism, record design, implementation, operating and tested-effectiveness assertions separately, bind assessment and evidence references, and explain the resulting contribution to residual risk under declared ownership.
model.scope_statement: A composable mixin adding a risk-and-control assurance surface to any host subject (system, process, service, supplier, asset, product). Its combined boundary has three parts. Risk projection: subject-scoped references to risk statements held in an external register plus the subject-specific parameters needed to reason about them here. Control linkage and effectiveness: a revision-pinned reference to an authoritative control catalogue entry, its classification and applicability projection, the many-to-many risk-to-control coverage graph, dependency and reliance edges, and five separately recorded states (existence, design adequacy, implementation, operation, tested effectiveness) bound to assessment method, timing and evidence references with integrity digests and an explicit validity window. Governance: owner, operator, assessor and approver references, controlled vocabularies, provenance and supersession discipline, access and disclosure rules, and the retention class applied to assertion records. The model is format-neutral; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of one record graph. It holds references, versions, digests and locally authored assertions only, and never reproduces the content or lifecycle of the catalogue, policy, configuration, test, evidence, remediation or audit models it points at.
in_scope: Subject-scoped reference to a risk statement, with response type and exposure scope parameters, resolved against an external risk register
Revision-pinned reference to one authoritative control catalogue entry, including selected parameter values and declared tailoring
Control objective statement and classification projection: preventive/detective/corrective, manual/automated/hybrid, entity-level or process-level, key or non-key
Applicability, in-scope population and not-applicable determinations with justification and approval reference
Directed risk-to-control linkage records carrying the claimed treatment mechanism and the basis of the claim
Many-to-many coverage topology, coverage completeness and precision notes, uncovered risks and unlinked controls
Control dependency and reliance edges, including reliance on general IT controls, shared services and inherited responsibility
External framework crosswalks with relation strength and an explicit non-conformance disclaimer
Design adequacy assertion, separate from implementation status, operating status and tested effectiveness
Implementation status, deviations, approved exceptions with expiry, and compensating or alternative control references
Declared operating frequency, event triggers, expected and observed occurrence counts for a stated period
Assessment method, depth and coverage, sample basis, assessment timing and assessor reference
Evidence references with integrity digests, sufficiency rationale and collection/expiry times
Effectiveness conclusion on a named vocabulary, with basis references, confidence, validity window and invalidation triggers
Deficiency severity value and a reference to the external record that tracks remediation
Residual risk contribution attribution, its method and effective date, and a reference to the acceptance decision
Ownership, operator, assessor and approver references plus independence flags
Controlled vocabulary declarations, provenance stamping, supersession and retention class of the assertion records themselves
out_of_scope: Authoring, versioning or publication of the control catalogue, its families, enhancements, parameter definitions or baselines
Policy and procedure text and its drafting, approval and publication lifecycle
Technical configuration, hardening baseline definitions and observed configuration state
Test case definition, test execution and raw test result records
Evidence object storage, chain of custody, integrity maintenance and evidence retention execution
Issue, deficiency and remediation workflow state machines, milestones and closure decisions
Audit engagement records, access logs and audit-trail immutability semantics
Runtime policy evaluation, control enforcement and blocking decisions by any engine
Enterprise risk taxonomy authorship, risk scoring methodology, appetite and tolerance threshold setting
Incident, loss event and near-miss records
Party and organisation master data, credentialing and identity proofing
Records-retention schedule authorship and execution of disposition
Control cost/benefit analysis, control rationalisation and portfolio optimisation

boundary_notes.distinction: That model owns control text, families, enhancements, parameter definitions, baselines and catalogue revisions. This mixin carries only a resolvable control reference pinned to a catalogue source and revision, the selected parameter values and declared tailoring for one subject.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Risk statement and risk register model
boundary_notes.distinction: That model owns risk identification, analysis, scoring, appetite and tolerance, the residual value and the acceptance decision. This mixin carries the risk reference, the claimed treatment mechanism and the attributed contribution, and never computes or stores the authoritative residual value.
That model owns policy and procedure documents and their approval lifecycle. Here a documented policy is only a reference; its existence never sets design, implementation or effectiveness values.

That model owns configuration definitions and observed system state. This mixin records that a control is implemented by a referenced component or configuration, not the configuration content or its drift detection.

That model owns assessment procedures, test cases, execution runs and raw results. This mixin binds a reference to an assessment plus its method, depth, timing and assessor, and never executes or re-derives a test.

That model owns evidence artefacts, custody, integrity maintenance and evidence retention. This mixin stores only the evidence reference, the digest asserted at binding time and a sufficiency rationale.
That model owns the remediation workflow, milestones, owners and closure. This mixin records a deficiency severity value and a reference to the tracking record; it holds no workflow state.

That model owns audit records, access logs and immutability guarantees. This mixin emits access and change events to it and retains only the emission reference; referencing an audit record grants no audit-trail semantics here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Runtime enforcement, monitoring and telemetry model
boundary_notes.distinction: That model owns policy evaluation, enforcement decisions and continuous monitoring feeds. This mixin declares expected cadence and consumes counts by reference; it never evaluates, enforces or blocks.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Party, role and organisation directory model
boundary_notes.distinction: That model owns party identity and role definitions. This mixin carries role-scoped references and independence flags for owner, operator, assessor and approver only.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.version_or_date: Revision 5, September 2020, updated through Release 5.2.0 (27 August 2025)
sources.relevance: Authoritative control catalogue structure: control identifiers, base controls and enhancements, parameters, related controls, families, tailoring and baselines; source for revision-pinned control reference semantics.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53A Rev. 5, Assessing Security and Privacy Controls in Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.version_or_date: Revision 5, January 2022, assessment procedures updated in Release 5.2.0 (August 2025)
sources.relevance: Assessment methodology and tailorable assessment procedures applied across the life cycle; anchors the separation of control implementation from assessed effectiveness.

sources.title: OSCAL Implementation Layer: Component Definition Model
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Machine-readable pattern for asserting which controls a component supports: control-implementation with source and set-parameters, implemented-requirement keyed to control-id, capability grouping, responsible roles, and mandatory UUID/last-modified change discipline.

sources.title: OSCAL Assessment Layer: Assessment Results Model
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Structures for reviewed-controls, observations with relevant evidence and collection/expiry, findings carrying objective and implementation status, risks with mitigating factors and remediations, and explicit result expiration.

sources.title: OSCAL Implementation Layer: System Security Plan Model
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Implemented-requirement and by-component structures, implementation-status values (implemented, partial, planned, not applicable), inherited/provided/responsibility splits and statement-level granularity.

sources.title: OSCAL Assessment Layer: Assessment Plan Model
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Control selection and objective selection for scoping, assessment subjects and assets, and task timing expressed on-date, within-date-range or at-frequency; anchors frequency and trigger declarations.

sources.title: AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements
sources.version_or_date: AS 2201 as published in the PCAOB standards library; amendments noted effective 15 December 2026
sources.relevance: Regulator-set distinction between testing design effectiveness and operating effectiveness; deficiency, significant deficiency and material weakness; nature, timing and extent of tests; evidence sufficiency proportional to control risk; compensating control precision; benchmarking of automated controls; rollforward from interim testing.

sources.title: Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government (Green Book), GAO-25-107721
sources.relevance: Current edition of the federal internal-control standards: management responsibility at all levels, documentation of risk assessment and response, change assessment, prioritisation of preventive control activities, and harmonisation with COSO.

sources.title: Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government (Green Book), GAO-14-704G
sources.version_or_date: GAO-14-704G, September 2014, effective fiscal year 2016; superseded by GAO-25-107721
sources.relevance: Full text source for the preventive versus detective control-activity distinction, documentation of control responsibilities in policies, the requirement that components operate together in an integrated manner, and deficiency identification and remediation.

sources.title: NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1, Integrating Cybersecurity and Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Cybersecurity risk register and risk detail record schemas, risk response selection, aggregation of lower-level risk into an enterprise risk profile, and the residual position that control effectiveness feeds.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Implement step requiring documentation of control deployment and deviations, Assess step with assessor objectivity, plan of action and milestones as the remediation vehicle, and ongoing authorization with continuous monitoring of control effectiveness.

sources.title: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Outcome taxonomy that links to external practices and controls through informative references without prescribing implementation; basis for treating crosswalks as alignment rather than conformance.

sources.title: NIST Computer Security Resource Center Glossary: compensating security control
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.version_or_date: CSRC glossary entry citing NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1, SP 800-39 and SP 800-137; accessed September 2026
sources.relevance: Normative definition of a compensating control as an alternative to a baseline control providing equivalent or comparable protection; distinguishes the NIST sense from the audit-deficiency sense.

sources.title: NIST Computer Security Resource Center Glossary: assessment method
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.version_or_date: CSRC glossary entry citing NIST SP 800-53A Rev. 5, SP 800-137, SP 800-137A and SP 800-79-2; accessed September 2026
sources.relevance: Defines the three assessment methods (examine, interview, test) that assessors use to obtain evidence; supplies the controlled vocabulary for the assessment-method field.

sources.title: Introduction to the Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF) v4.0
sources.organization: National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), United Kingdom
sources.version_or_date: CAF v4.0, published 18 April 2024, reviewed 6 August 2025
sources.relevance: Objective/principle/contributing-outcome/indicator hierarchy with achieved, partially achieved and not achieved values, and an explicit warning against tick-box assessment; supplies an alternative outcome vocabulary and supports the mapping-is-not-effectiveness rule.

sources.title: Internal Control - Integrated Framework (ICIF-2013), guidance page
sources.organization: Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO)
sources.version_or_date: Framework originally issued 1992, refreshed 2013 (ICIF-2013); page accessed September 2026
sources.relevance: Confirms the five components, seventeen principles and the criterion that effective internal control requires all principles present and functioning. Limited evidence: the full framework text is paywalled and was not retrieved.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0: Compensating Controls vs Customized Approach
sources.version_or_date: Published 18 July 2022, referring to PCI DSS v4.0
sources.relevance: Standards-body statement that a compensating control requires a legitimate and documented technical or business constraint, cannot be applied retroactively, and is distinct from a customized approach requiring a targeted risk analysis; the two cannot be combined for the same requirement.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-137, Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) for Federal Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Visibility into the effectiveness of deployed controls, determination of assessment frequency from criticality and volatility, ongoing assessment in place of periodic snapshots and reuse of assessment results.

sources.title: Revisions to the Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk
sources.organization: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), Bank for International Settlements
sources.relevance: Supervisory operational-risk principles aligned to the Basel III operational risk framework with updated change-management and ICT guidance; the Committee's 2014 review finding that several principles had not been adequately implemented supports treating documentation as no evidence of implementation. Limited evidence: only the publication landing page was retrievable.

bundles.name: Control reference, classification and applicability
bundles.description: What control is being talked about, how it is characterised, where it applies to the host subject, and who is accountable for it.
bundles.rationale: Every downstream assertion about linkage, implementation and effectiveness is meaningless unless the control is bound to one authoritative catalogue entry at a known revision, classified on declared vocabularies, scoped to a stated population and attached to named accountable parties. NIST SP 800-53 and the OSCAL implementation layer both key implementation assertions to a control identifier resolved against a named catalogue source, and the internal-control standards make management responsibility and documented scoping a precondition of any effectiveness claim.

layers.name: Authoritative control reference and characterisation
layers.description: The revision-pinned binding to an external control definition, and the objective and classification facets projected onto it for this subject.

findings.name: Authoritative control reference and revision binding
findings.description: Binds this assertion set to exactly one control definition in an external catalogue, pinned to a named catalogue source and revision, with the parameter values selected and any tailoring declared for the host subject. Catalogue text, families, enhancements and parameter definitions remain owned by the catalogue model.

questions.text: Which single authoritative catalogue entry does this assertion set bind to, and under which identifier scheme?
answer_data: Control identifier as issued by the catalogue

questions.text: Which catalogue release or revision was in force when the binding was made, and how is that pin preserved?
answer_data: Digest of the referenced catalogue entry at pin time

questions.text: Which control statement parts or enhancements are in scope for this binding, and which parameter values were selected?
answer_data: Parameter identifier and selected value pairs

questions.text: What tailoring or deviation from the catalogue baseline does this binding assert, and on whose authority?
How can a consumer resolve this binding without importing the catalogue text into local storage?

data_elements.name: Control reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the authoritative control definition, carried in the issuing catalogue's namespace.

data_elements.name: Catalogue source reference
data_elements.description: Identifier or URI of the catalogue, profile or baseline from which the control reference is drawn.

data_elements.name: Catalogue revision pin
data_elements.description: Release, revision or version label of the catalogue in force at binding time.

data_elements.name: Selected parameter values
data_elements.description: Parameter identifier and value pairs chosen for this subject, mirroring catalogue parameter definitions without redefining them.

data_elements.name: Binding observation time
data_elements.description: Time at which the binding was captured into this model, distinct from any catalogue publication date.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding is a pure reference binding. Its whole content is an external identifier, a catalogue source, a revision pin, parameter selections and a digest; the control definition itself is an artifact of the catalogue model and reproducing it locally would duplicate a target-owned lifecycle.

findings.name: Control objective and classification projection
findings.description: The objective the control is claimed to achieve for the host subject plus classification facets: functional type (preventive, detective, corrective), execution mode (manual, automated, hybrid), operating level (entity or process/transaction) and key designation. Values are source-qualified; where a catalogue publishes its own attribute values they are carried unchanged.

questions.text: What control objective is the control claimed to achieve for this specific host subject?
answer_data: Reference to the catalogue objective it specialises

questions.text: Is the control preventive, detective or corrective, and which vocabulary and source supply that value?
Is the control executed manually, automatically or as a hybrid, and which part is automated?
Does the control operate at entity level or at process and transaction level for this subject?
Has the control been designated key or non-key for this subject, and who made that determination?

data_elements.name: Subject control objective
data_elements.description: Locally authored statement of what the control is claimed to achieve for this subject.

data_elements.name: Functional type
data_elements.description: Preventive, detective or corrective classification; multi-valued where a control acts in more than one mode.

data_elements.name: Execution mode
data_elements.description: Manual, automated or hybrid execution of the control.

data_elements.name: Operating level
data_elements.description: Entity-level or process/transaction-level operation of the control.

data_elements.name: Key control designation
data_elements.description: Whether the control is designated key for the subject, with the determining party recorded in provenance.

data_elements.name: Classification vocabulary reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the controlled vocabulary each classification value is drawn from.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is a small set of source-qualified coded values projected onto an externally owned control definition. It carries no document of its own, and materialising it as an artifact would invite it to drift from the catalogue attributes it qualifies.

layers.name: Applicability, scope and accountability
layers.description: Whether and where the control applies to the host subject, and which parties own, operate, assess and approve the assertions about it.

findings.name: Applicability, covered population and exclusion determination
findings.description: Declares whether the control applies to the host subject, the population or boundary it covers, the basis for that determination, and any not-applicable or partially applicable determination with justification, approval and validity window.

questions.text: Does this control apply to the host subject, and on what documented basis was that determined?
What population, boundary or component set does the control cover within the subject?
If the control is declared not applicable or only partially applicable, what justification and approval support that?
From when until when does this applicability determination hold?
Which obligation or authority makes this control mandatory rather than discretionary for the subject?

data_elements.name: Applicability status
data_elements.description: Applicable, partially applicable or not applicable determination for the subject.

data_elements.name: Applicability basis
data_elements.description: Documented reason the control applies, including scoping rule or obligation reference.

data_elements.name: Covered population reference
data_elements.description: References to the components, records or process instances the control is claimed to cover.

data_elements.name: Exclusion justification
data_elements.description: Justification recorded when applicability is denied or narrowed, with approver in provenance.

data_elements.name: Applicability effective-from
data_elements.description: Event time from which the applicability determination holds, distinct from the time it was recorded.

artifacts.name: Control applicability statement
artifacts.description: A versioned, subject-scoped statement of applicability recording, per control, the applicability status, basis, covered population, exclusion justification and approval. It is the reviewable unit that scoping and certification consumers read.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system applicability record identifier where the adopting Dimension operates a governance system of record; otherwise a governed IRI in the Dimension namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID minted at first record. No date, control title or framework code is used as the identifier.

findings.name: Owner, operator, assessor and approver references
findings.description: Role-scoped references to the parties accountable for the control and its assertions, including shared, provided and inherited responsibility splits, competence and authority assertions for the performer, and independence flags for the assessor and approver. Party master data stays in the directory model.

questions.text: Which party is accountable for the control's continued operation for this subject?
Who is authorised to approve the effectiveness conclusion, and are they independent of the operator?
How is responsibility divided between the subject owner, a shared service and any external provider?
What competence and authority are asserted for the party performing the control?
Which parties may read or amend this control assertion set, and under which role?

data_elements.name: Control owner reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the accountable owner party or organisational unit.

data_elements.name: Control operator reference
data_elements.description: References to the parties or systems that perform the control.

data_elements.name: Assessor reference
data_elements.description: References to the parties that assess the control, with independence recorded separately.

data_elements.name: Responsibility split
data_elements.description: Structured allocation of provided, inherited and customer responsibility across parties.

data_elements.name: Assessor independence flag
data_elements.description: Whether the assessing or approving party is independent of the party operating the control.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Accountability here is a set of role-scoped pointers into the party and organisation directory plus two local qualifiers. Holding it inline prevents this model from becoming a shadow party register with its own identity lifecycle.

bundles.name: Risk-to-control linkage, coverage and framework alignment
bundles.description: The graph that connects risk statements to controls, the aggregate coverage it produces, dependency edges between controls, and crosswalks to other frameworks that carry no conformance meaning.
bundles.rationale: The registered purpose of this mixin is risk-control linkage, and linkage semantics must be stated explicitly rather than implied by co-location. NIST IR 8286 and SP 800-37 tie controls to a risk response and to the residual position that rolls up into an enterprise risk profile, the internal-control standards derive control activities from an assessed risk, and CSF 2.0 and the NCSC CAF establish that a mapping between frameworks is an alignment and not evidence of an achieved outcome.

layers.name: Treatment linkage and coverage topology
layers.description: Individual risk-to-control links with their claimed treatment mechanism, and the aggregate many-to-many coverage and dependency structure they form.

findings.name: Risk-to-control link and claimed treatment mechanism
findings.description: One directed link from a risk statement reference to a control reference, carrying the claimed treatment mechanism, the risk-response type it serves, any claimed magnitude of reduction, the basis of the claim and its provenance. The risk record and its own lifecycle stay in the risk model.

questions.text: Which risk statement does this control link to, and in which direction does the treatment claim run?
By what mechanism is the control claimed to treat the risk: likelihood, impact, detection latency or transfer support?
What magnitude of reduction is claimed, on what scale, and is the claim estimated or demonstrated?
answer_data: Claim basis code: estimated, analysed or tested

questions.text: Who asserted this linkage, from which analysis, and at what event and observation times?
answer_data: Event time and observation time in RFC 3339

questions.text: What causes this linkage to be superseded or retired, and how is the prior link preserved?

data_elements.name: Risk statement reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the risk record in the owning risk register.

data_elements.name: Claimed treatment mechanism
data_elements.description: How the control is claimed to act on the risk: reduce likelihood, reduce impact, shorten detection or containment time, or support transfer.

data_elements.name: Risk response type served
data_elements.description: The risk response the link serves, drawn from the risk model's response vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Claim basis
data_elements.description: Whether the treatment claim is estimated, analytically derived or demonstrated by testing.

data_elements.name: Link assertion event time
data_elements.description: Event time at which the linkage was asserted, recorded separately from the ingestion time of the record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A link is a relationship assertion between two externally owned records. Both endpoints are artifacts of other models, so the only local content is the qualified edge itself, which is best held as inline reference data that can be traversed without materialising a document.

findings.name: Many-to-many coverage and control dependency structure
findings.description: The aggregate view over links: which control sets cover which risks and vice versa, coverage completeness and precision, uncovered risks and unlinked controls, plus dependency and reliance edges between controls including reliance on general IT controls, shared services and inherited controls.

questions.text: Which controls together are claimed to cover a given risk, and can any one of them cover it alone?
At what level of precision does the control set operate relative to the risk it is claimed to cover?
Which other controls must operate for this control to be effective, and what happens when they fail?
Which linked risks currently have no operating control, and which controls have no linked risk?
How is the coverage set expressed so a consumer can traverse it without loading the full catalogue?

data_elements.name: Coverage edge set
data_elements.description: The set of risk-to-control edges scoped to the host subject, each carrying a sufficiency flag.

data_elements.name: Coverage completeness
data_elements.description: Assessed completeness of the control set against the linked risk, on a declared vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Coverage precision note
data_elements.description: Statement of the level of precision at which the control set acts relative to the risk.

data_elements.name: Control dependency reference
data_elements.description: References to controls, shared services or inherited controls this control relies on, with dependency type.

data_elements.name: Uncovered risk reference
data_elements.description: References to in-scope risks with no linked control in an operating state.

artifacts.name: Risk-to-control coverage matrix
artifacts.description: A versioned projection of the many-to-many coverage and dependency graph for one host subject, showing per-risk control sets, sufficiency flags, dependency edges, uncovered risks and unlinked controls at a stated evaluation time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system matrix identifier where a governance system of record issues one; otherwise a governed IRI in the Dimension namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID minted at first generation. The evaluation time is an attribute, never part of the identifier.

layers.name: External framework alignment
layers.description: Secondary mappings from the bound control to entries in other catalogues and outcome frameworks, held strictly as alignment.

findings.name: Framework crosswalk without conformance claim
findings.description: Mappings from the bound control to entries in other frameworks, each carrying relation strength, the target framework version, the mapping author and date, and an explicit disclaimer that the mapping asserts alignment only and never conformance, implementation or effectiveness.

questions.text: To which entries in other frameworks is this control mapped, and with what relation strength?
answer_data: Relation strength code: equivalent, subset, superset, related, no-match

questions.text: Who authored each mapping, against which target framework version, and when?
What does this mapping explicitly not assert about conformance, implementation or effectiveness?
How is a mapping revalidated when either the source or the target framework version changes?

data_elements.name: Crosswalk target reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an entry in another catalogue or outcome framework.

data_elements.name: Crosswalk relation strength
data_elements.description: Declared relation between the bound control and the target entry.

data_elements.name: Crosswalk target version
data_elements.description: Version label of the target framework the mapping was authored against.

data_elements.name: Non-conformance disclaimer
data_elements.description: Mandatory flag asserting that the mapping establishes alignment only and confers no conformance or effectiveness meaning.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Crosswalks are pure reference data pointing at externally governed framework entries. Publishing them as a local artifact would encourage downstream consumers to treat a mapping table as an assurance deliverable, which is precisely the inference this model forbids.

bundles.name: Design, implementation, operation, evidence and tested effectiveness
bundles.description: The five separately recorded states of a control for the host subject, the assessment and evidence that support them, and the contribution the result makes to residual risk.
bundles.rationale: Every consulted assurance source separates the question of whether a control is designed adequately from whether it is implemented, whether it operates and whether its operation has been tested. PCAOB AS 2201 distinguishes design testing from operating-effectiveness testing and grades deficiencies accordingly; SP 800-53A and OSCAL separate implementation status from assessed objective status and attach expiry to results; the internal-control standards require components to be present and functioning rather than merely documented. Collapsing these states is the single most common failure this bundle exists to prevent.

layers.name: Design, implementation and operating assertions
layers.description: Three distinct status assertions about the control for this subject, each with its own basis, determining party and time, and none derivable from another.

findings.name: Design adequacy assertion
findings.description: The assertion that the control, if operated as prescribed, would achieve its objective: design status, design rationale, the threshold or precision at which it would act, the determining party and time, and any recorded design limitation or design deficiency reference. Explicitly independent of whether the control is implemented or operating.

questions.text: What is the current design status of the control for this subject, and what does that value deliberately exclude?
If operated exactly as prescribed, which part of the objective would the control achieve and which part would it not?
At what threshold, tolerance or level of precision is the control designed to act?
Who determined that the design is adequate, on what date, and against which criteria?
What known design limitation or design deficiency is recorded, and which external record tracks it?

data_elements.name: Design status
data_elements.description: Assertion of design adequacy on a declared vocabulary, independent of implementation and operation.

data_elements.name: Design rationale
data_elements.description: Locally authored reasoning for the design determination, referencing but not reproducing the procedure or configuration.

data_elements.name: Design precision or threshold
data_elements.description: The threshold, tolerance or precision at which the control is designed to act.

data_elements.name: Design determination event time
data_elements.description: Event time of the design determination, recorded separately from ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Design deficiency reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a record in the deficiency and remediation model describing a design shortfall.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The design description itself lives in the policy, procedure or configuration model. What is asserted here is a status, a rationale and a threshold, and keeping it inline makes clear that this model judges an externally owned design rather than publishing one.

findings.name: Implementation state, deviations, exceptions and compensating controls
findings.description: Whether the designed control is actually in place for the subject: implementation status and scope of partial implementation, recorded deviations from the design, approved exceptions or waivers with expiry, and references to compensating or alternative controls together with the documented constraint that justifies them. Compensating control definitions and remediation workflow stay in their owning models.

questions.text: What implementation status is recorded for the subject, and what scope does a partial status actually cover?
Which approved exception or waiver permits a gap in implementation, who approved it, and when does it expire?
Which compensating or alternative control is relied on, and against which defined requirement?
answer_data: Compensating-sense code distinguishing baseline-alternative from deficiency-mitigating

questions.text: What documented technical or business constraint justifies the compensating or alternative approach?
Which change to the subject last altered the implementation state, and when was that change recorded?
answer_data: Observation time of the resulting assertion

data_elements.name: Implementation status
data_elements.description: Status such as implemented, partial, planned, alternative implementation or not applicable, drawn from a declared vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Deviation record
data_elements.description: Recorded departures from the designed implementation, each with a reason and approval reference.

data_elements.name: Exception or waiver reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an approved exception permitting non-implementation, held in the governance model.

data_elements.name: Exception expiry
data_elements.description: Time at which the approved exception lapses and the gap reverts to unmitigated.

data_elements.name: Compensating control reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the compensating or alternative control relied on, with an explicit sense code.

data_elements.name: Documented constraint
data_elements.description: The technical or business constraint that justifies a compensating or alternative approach.

artifacts.name: Control implementation assertion record
artifacts.description: A versioned record stating, for one control and one host subject, the implementation status, partial scope, deviations, exceptions with expiry, and compensating or alternative control references with their justifying constraint.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system assertion identifier where a governance system of record issues one; otherwise a governed IRI in the Dimension namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID minted at first assertion. Revision is a separate integer, never encoded as a date.

findings.name: Operating status, frequency and triggers
findings.description: How the control actually runs: operating status kept distinct from implementation status, declared frequency or event triggers, the expected occurrence population for a stated period, observed occurrence counts obtained by reference, and suspension or dormancy handling. Execution records belong to the executing system.

questions.text: Is the control currently operating, and how does that value differ from being implemented?
At what frequency, or on which event triggers, is the control expected to operate?
answer_data: Timing form: on-date, within-date-range or at-frequency

questions.text: How many occurrences were expected and how many observed in the stated period?
answer_data: Period start and end in RFC 3339

questions.text: Which system or party executes the control, and where is that execution recorded?
What suspends or resumes operation of the control, and how is a dormant period represented?

data_elements.name: Operating status
data_elements.description: Whether the control is operating, suspended or not operating, distinct from implementation status.

data_elements.name: Operating frequency
data_elements.description: Declared cadence at which the control is expected to operate.

data_elements.name: Operating trigger
data_elements.description: Events that cause the control to operate where it is not periodic.

data_elements.name: Expected occurrence count
data_elements.description: Population of expected control occurrences in the stated period.

data_elements.name: Observed occurrence count
data_elements.description: Count of occurrences obtained by reference from the executing system, with its retrieval time.

data_elements.name: Operating period
data_elements.description: Start and end of the period over which operation is claimed, both RFC 3339 with offset.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Execution records, logs and telemetry are produced and owned by the executing system and the monitoring model. Only the declared cadence, trigger set and referenced counts belong here, and holding them inline keeps this model from accreting an operational record store.

layers.name: Assessment and evidence binding
layers.description: The binding between an effectiveness assertion and the assessment activity and evidence objects that support it, held as references, methods, times and digests only.

findings.name: Assessment method, timing and evidence binding
findings.description: Binds an effectiveness assertion to the assessment activity and its evidence: assessment method (examine, interview, test), depth and coverage attributes, sample or population basis, assessment event time and the operating period covered, assessor reference, and evidence references with integrity digests, collection times and expiry. Test cases, results and evidence payloads remain in their owning models.

questions.text: Which evidence objects support the assertion, and how is each referenced and integrity-bound?
answer_data: Digest value and algorithm at binding time

questions.text: Which assessment methods were applied, and at what depth and coverage?
When was the assessment performed, and which period of control operation does its conclusion cover?
answer_data: Observation or ingestion time of the binding

questions.text: Why is the bound evidence sufficient given the risk associated with this control?
If testing was performed at an interim date, what supports extending the conclusion to the end of the period?

data_elements.name: Assessment reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assessment plan, activity or result record in the owning assessment model.

data_elements.name: Assessment method
data_elements.description: One or more of examine, interview and test, as defined by the assessment vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Depth and coverage attributes
data_elements.description: Rigour and breadth attributes attached to the applied assessment methods.

data_elements.name: Sample basis
data_elements.description: Population, sample size and selection method used for the assessment.

data_elements.name: Assessment event time
data_elements.description: Event time at which the assessment was performed, distinct from the binding's ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an evidence object held by the evidence model.

data_elements.name: Evidence integrity digest
data_elements.description: Digest asserted by the owning evidence model at binding time, with algorithm identifier.

artifacts.name: Assessment and evidence binding manifest
artifacts.description: A versioned manifest listing, for one effectiveness assertion, the assessment references, applied methods, depth and coverage, sample basis, timing, assessor reference and each bound evidence reference with its digest and collection time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system manifest identifier where an assessment system of record issues one; otherwise a governed IRI in the Dimension namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID minted at first binding. Assessment dates are attributes, never identifier components.

layers.name: Tested effectiveness and residual contribution
layers.description: The conclusion drawn about operating effectiveness with its confidence and expiry, and the contribution that conclusion makes to the residual position of the linked risk.

findings.name: Tested effectiveness conclusion, confidence and validity
findings.description: The conclusion about operating effectiveness on a named vocabulary, with its scope, the assessment and evidence bindings that are its only permitted basis, an attached confidence and its limits, a validity window with invalidation triggers, and any deficiency severity with a reference to the record tracking remediation.

questions.text: What effectiveness conclusion was reached, on which named vocabulary, and over what scope?
Which assessment and evidence bindings form the sole permitted basis for this conclusion?
What confidence is attached to the conclusion, and what limits that confidence?
Until when is the conclusion valid, and which events invalidate it before that time?
If the conclusion is adverse, what deficiency severity is recorded and which external record tracks remediation?

data_elements.name: Effectiveness conclusion
data_elements.description: Conclusion value on a named vocabulary, never derived from documentation, mapping or incident absence.

data_elements.name: Conclusion vocabulary
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the vocabulary the conclusion value is drawn from.

data_elements.name: Conclusion basis reference
data_elements.description: References to the assessment and evidence binding manifests that support the conclusion.

data_elements.name: Conclusion confidence
data_elements.description: Declared confidence in the conclusion together with the factors limiting it.

data_elements.name: Conclusion validity expiry
data_elements.description: Time after which the conclusion is no longer current and degrades to unknown.

data_elements.name: Deficiency severity
data_elements.description: Severity value recorded for an adverse conclusion, on the declared severity vocabulary.

artifacts.name: Control effectiveness conclusion statement
artifacts.description: A versioned statement recording the effectiveness conclusion for one control and subject, its vocabulary, scope, basis references, confidence, validity window, invalidation triggers, deficiency severity and approving party.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system conclusion identifier where an assurance system of record issues one; otherwise a governed IRI in the Dimension namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID minted at first conclusion. Validity dates are attributes, never identifier components.

findings.name: Residual contribution and acceptance linkage
findings.description: How the assessed effectiveness of this control contributes to the residual position of the linked risk: the attributed change from inherent to residual, the attribution method and its effective time, the attribution status, and references to the residual risk record and any acceptance decision. Residual values, appetite thresholds and acceptance decisions are owned by the risk model.

questions.text: What change from the inherent to the residual position is attributed to this control, and on which scale?
Which effectiveness conclusion and which attribution method produced the attributed change?
Which residual risk record does this contribution feed, and has the risk model accepted the attribution?
What prevents an untested or ineffective control from reducing the recorded residual position?
When the supporting conclusion expires, what happens to this residual contribution?

data_elements.name: Residual risk record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the residual risk record in the owning risk model that this contribution feeds.

data_elements.name: Attributed reduction
data_elements.description: Quantified or ordinal change from inherent to residual attributed to this control.

data_elements.name: Attribution method
data_elements.description: Method used to derive the attributed change, drawn from a declared vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Attribution status
data_elements.description: Whether the attribution is claimed, accepted by the risk owner, suspended on expiry or rejected.

data_elements.name: Attribution effective time
data_elements.description: Event time from which the attribution applies, recorded separately from ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Acceptance decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the risk acceptance or authorization decision recorded in the risk model.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The residual value, the appetite thresholds and the acceptance decision are all owned by the risk model. What is held here is an attribution claim plus pointers, and publishing it as an artifact would create a second, competing statement of residual risk.

functions.name: Link risk to control
functions.description: Create a directed risk-to-control link carrying the claimed treatment mechanism, the risk response type it serves and the basis of the claim.
inputs: Control reference with catalogue source and revision pin
Treatment mechanism code and claim basis
Asserting party reference and event time
outputs: Persisted link record with local identifier
Updated coverage edge set for the host subject
preconditions: Both endpoints resolve in their owning models
The control reference is pinned to a named catalogue revision
The treatment mechanism value exists in the declared vocabulary
effects: A new link record is added with event time and observation time recorded separately
The coverage matrix projection is marked stale for regeneration
No risk score, residual value or control definition is modified

functions.name: Retire risk-to-control link
functions.description: Retire or supersede an existing link without destroying it, recording the reason and any replacement link.
outputs: Link record marked superseded or retired
preconditions: The link record exists and is not already retired
The actor holds a write role for linkage records
effects: The prior link remains readable with superseded-at timestamp and reason
Any residual contribution depending on the link is suspended
The remediation workflow in the owning model is notified by reference only

functions.name: Record control applicability
functions.description: Record or revise an applicability, partial-applicability or not-applicable determination for a control against the host subject, with basis, covered population and approval.
inputs: Applicability status, basis and covered population references
Approving party reference and effective-from time
outputs: New revision of the control applicability statement
Updated applicability status on the assertion set
preconditions: The control reference resolves and is revision-pinned
A not-applicable or partial status carries a justification and an approver
effects: A serial applicability statement revision is created; the prior revision remains readable
Dependent implementation and effectiveness assertions are flagged for review
Scoping authority and obligation records in other models are unchanged

functions.name: Record design, implementation and operating assertion
functions.description: Record or revise the three state assertions for a control and subject, each with its own basis, determining party and event time, including deviations, exceptions and compensating control references.
inputs: Control reference and host subject reference
Implementation status, deviations, exception and compensating control references
Determining party reference and event time
outputs: New revision of the control implementation assertion record
Independent design, implementation and operating status values
preconditions: Applicability is recorded as applicable or partially applicable
Each status value exists in its declared vocabulary
A compensating control reference carries a sense code and a documented constraint
effects: Three status values are stored independently; none is derived from another
Any dependent effectiveness conclusion is marked for revalidation
No policy text, procedure or configuration is created or altered

functions.name: Bind assessment and evidence references
functions.description: Bind assessment references, applied methods, depth, coverage, sample basis, timing and assessor to a control assertion, together with evidence references and their integrity digests.
inputs: Assessment reference, method codes, depth and coverage
Sample basis and covered operating period
Evidence references with digests and collection times
Assessor reference and assessment event time
outputs: New revision of the assessment and evidence binding manifest
Digest verification result per bound evidence reference
preconditions: Every assessment and evidence reference resolves in its owning model
Each method code is one of examine, interview or test
The assessor reference is present and its independence flag is set
effects: References and digests are stored; no evidence payload, test case or test result is copied or executed
A digest mismatch marks the binding unverified and blocks its use as a conclusion basis
Evidence retention and custody remain governed by the evidence model

functions.name: Record effectiveness conclusion
functions.description: Record an effectiveness conclusion with its vocabulary, scope, basis references, confidence, validity window, invalidation triggers and any deficiency severity.
inputs: Valid-until time, invalidation triggers, optional deficiency severity
outputs: New revision of the control effectiveness conclusion statement
Expiry schedule entry for the conclusion
preconditions: At least one verified assessment or evidence binding manifest resolves
The approving party is distinct from the operating party where independence is required
The conclusion vocabulary is declared and versioned
effects: The conclusion is stored with its basis references and cannot be created without them
Conclusions derived from documentation, framework mapping or incident absence are rejected
On reaching valid-until the conclusion is read as expired rather than effective
Deficiency remediation is tracked by reference only, in the owning model

functions.name: Explain residual contribution
functions.description: Produce a traceable explanation of how a control's assessed effectiveness contributes to the residual position of a linked risk, and submit the attribution to the risk model.
outputs: Residual contribution record with attributed change and status
Explanation trace from evidence binding through conclusion to attribution
preconditions: A non-expired effectiveness conclusion exists for the linked control
The attribution method is declared and the risk model exposes a compatible scale
The link record is active and not superseded
effects: An attribution claim is recorded with status claimed until the risk owner accepts it
An untested, expired or adverse conclusion yields no reduction attribution
The authoritative residual value, appetite thresholds and acceptance decision remain computed and owned by the risk model

composition.purpose: Inherit record metadata, versioning, change-detection and provenance obligations that every control assertion record must satisfy, rather than restating them locally.

composition.target: Host subject model (system, process, service, supplier, asset or product to which this mixin attaches)
composition.purpose: Attach the risk-and-control assurance surface to a subject without altering that subject's own identity, classification or lifecycle.

Resolve control definitions, families, enhancements, parameter definitions, baselines and revisions; this model carries the reference, revision pin, selected parameter values and declared tailoring only.

composition.target: Risk statement and risk register model
composition.purpose: Resolve risk statements, response types, appetite and tolerance, residual values and acceptance decisions; this model carries the risk reference, treatment claim and attributed contribution only.
Point at the policy or procedure that documents a control without importing its text or approval lifecycle, and without letting its existence set any status value here.
Identify the component or configuration by which a control is implemented, leaving configuration content, drift detection and enforcement in that model.
Bind assessment activities, methods and timing by reference; assessment procedures, test cases, execution and raw results stay in that model.
Bind evidence by reference and digest with a local sufficiency rationale; evidence payloads, custody, integrity maintenance and retention execution stay in that model.

composition.target: Issue, deficiency and remediation model (plan of action and milestones)
composition.purpose: Record a deficiency severity value and point at the record that tracks remediation; milestones, owners, workflow states and closure decisions stay in that model.
Emit access and change events and retain the emission reference; audit records, log retention and trail immutability semantics are owned entirely by that model.

composition.target: Party, role and organisation directory model
composition.purpose: Resolve owner, operator, assessor and approver identities; this model stores role-scoped references and independence flags only.

composition.target: Runtime enforcement, monitoring and telemetry model
composition.purpose: Obtain observed occurrence counts and monitoring signals by reference; policy evaluation, enforcement decisions and execution records remain owned there.

composition.target: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control catalogue with the OSCAL implementation and assessment layers
composition.purpose: Align local field semantics for control reference, parameter setting, implementation status, assessment method, finding and result expiry with a published machine-readable representation, without claiming conformance.

composition.target: COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework (ICIF-2013) and GAO Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government
composition.purpose: Align the design, implementation, operation and deficiency vocabulary with recognised internal-control criteria; the frameworks' own assessment of an entity's internal control remains external.

composition.target: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 outcome taxonomy and NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework outcomes
composition.purpose: Offer selectable outcome vocabularies for effectiveness conclusions and crosswalk targets, with an explicit rule that a mapping to an outcome is never evidence that the outcome is achieved.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one accountable owner for the WM-XCT-027 mixin package and one delegate per host-subject class before any linkage or assertion record is created.

The owner package declares which external models supply the control catalogue, risk register, assessment execution, evidence store, remediation tracking, audit trail and party directory, and records the resolution endpoint and version policy for each.

The owner package publishes and versions every controlled vocabulary used here: functional type, execution mode, applicability status, design status, implementation status, operating status, assessment method, effectiveness conclusion, confidence, deficiency severity, treatment mechanism and attribution method.

The owner package records the retention class, jurisdiction and independence requirements applicable to control assertions in each region where the Dimension operates, and names the policy that owns the disposition schedule.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local records are minted under a Dimension-governed namespace of the form {dimension-root}/xct/rsk/control/{local-id}. External control, risk, evidence, assessment and party identifiers are carried verbatim in their issuing namespace with an explicit source qualifier and are never re-minted, re-cased or normalised locally.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-027 (record plane world-model, model WM-XCT-027, nav path NAV.XCT.RSK, domain tag XCT.RSK)
Parent model registry entry WM-KNW-015 for inherited record metadata and provenance obligations
Dimension-local controlled vocabulary registry for every coded field named in the owner package requirements
External catalogue registries referenced by control bindings, including the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 catalogue and its OSCAL representations

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the format-neutral record graph; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB projections must round-trip to it without semantic loss.

Order-insensitive collections (coverage edges, crosswalk entries, evidence references, deviation records) are canonicalised by sorting on the external identifier first and the local identifier second.
All time values are normalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset before any digest is computed.
Coded values are canonicalised as a vocabulary identifier, vocabulary version and value triple, never as a bare string.
Free text is stored verbatim; whitespace normalisation is applied only when computing digests and never to the stored value.
patch_rules: Assertions are append-only: a superseding revision is written and the prior revision is marked superseded with a reason code, actor reference and RFC 3339 timestamp; values are never overwritten in place.

Any patch that changes the catalogue reference, revision pin, applicability status, design status, implementation status, operating status or effectiveness conclusion must carry an actor reference, an event time, an observation time and a reason code.
Patches touching evidence or assessment references must recompute and restate the integrity digest, and must mark the binding unverified on mismatch.
An expired effectiveness conclusion may not be patched; a new conclusion record with fresh basis references must be created instead.
Changing the catalogue revision pin cascades an invalidation flag onto dependent design, implementation and effectiveness assertions rather than silently carrying them forward.
compatibility_rules: Adding a value to a controlled vocabulary is a minor change; removing, renaming or redefining a value is breaking and requires a new vocabulary version plus a published migration map.
Consumers must ignore unknown optional fields, and must fail closed on an unknown required coded value rather than defaulting to an effective, implemented or applicable interpretation.
Redefining the meaning of any effectiveness conclusion, deficiency severity or implementation status value is always a breaking change.
Projections may add representation-specific fields but must not add semantics absent from the canonical record graph.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the artifact, such as a governance, assurance or assessment master, carried verbatim with its issuing namespace.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in the adopting Dimension's namespace where no master system issues an identifier.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension at first record, used only when neither a master-system identifier nor a governed IRI is available.
A date, a control title, a framework code, a risk name or a status value is never an identifier and may be carried only as a label or attribute.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded in RFC 3339 format with seconds precision and an explicit numeric offset or the literal Z. Event time (when the control operated, the assessment was performed, the determination was made or the exception was approved) is recorded in a separate field from observation or ingestion time (when the fact was captured into this model), and the two are never collapsed; where they are known to differ the record must carry both, and derived validity windows are computed from event time only.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts carry a stable series identifier plus a monotonically increasing integer revision, rendered as {series-id}.r{revision}. The label never encodes a date, a period, a status, a conclusion value or a framework code, and revision numbers are never reused after supersession or retirement.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each artifact revision stores a digest over its canonical form together with the algorithm identifier. For bound external evidence and assessment references the digest asserted by the owning model at binding time is stored alongside. A digest mismatch on read marks the binding unverified, invalidates any effectiveness conclusion that depends on it, and must be resolved by a new binding rather than by silent repair.

policies: Effectiveness is never inferred: an effectiveness conclusion may cite only verified assessment and evidence bindings, and may never be derived from the existence of documentation, from a framework mapping, from a control's presence in a catalogue or baseline, or from the absence of incidents or losses.

Existence, design adequacy, implementation, operation and tested effectiveness are five separate recorded values; no value may be automatically derived from another, and a read that returns one must not imply any other.
A control framework crosswalk is an alignment only and never establishes conformance; conformance claims require separately recorded evidence and are not produced by this model.
Expired effectiveness conclusions degrade to unknown on read and suspend any residual contribution that depends on them; they never persist as current.

Proprietary or paywalled framework content is referenced by identifier and version only and is never reproduced; where a vocabulary derives from paywalled material the record stores the local vocabulary and cites the external source without copying its text.
This model records, and never executes: it does not run tests, collect evidence, enforce controls, drive remediation workflow or maintain audit trails, all of which remain with their owning models.

read: Read resolves a control assertion set with its bound references, returning identifier, version and digest for external content without dereferencing catalogue, evidence, test-result or audit content into local storage.
Read of an effectiveness conclusion after its valid-until time returns an explicit expired marker alongside the stale value, never the value alone.
Read of a coverage matrix is permitted at layer scope for risk aggregation, subject to the access default rule and to redaction of security-sensitive control detail.
Read returns the vocabulary identifier and version for every coded value so a consumer can reject values it does not understand.
create: Creating a linkage record requires a resolvable risk reference, a control reference pinned to a named catalogue revision, a treatment mechanism value from the declared vocabulary, a claim basis and an actor reference.
Creating an effectiveness conclusion requires at least one verified assessment or evidence binding manifest; creation fails if none resolves or if all bound digests are unverified.
Creating a not-applicable or partial applicability determination requires a justification and an approving party reference.
Every created record stores event time and observation or ingestion time separately, both in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.
update: Updates are expressed as superseding revisions; the prior revision remains readable with its superseded-at timestamp, actor and reason code.
Changing the catalogue revision pin invalidates dependent design, implementation and effectiveness assertions, which must be re-asserted rather than carried forward.
Bulk vocabulary migration requires a published mapping and is recorded as a single provenance-stamped operation with a reversible migration record.
Updating an evidence or assessment binding recomputes the integrity digest and re-evaluates the verification state of every dependent conclusion.
delete: Records of this model are not hard-deleted by default: retirement writes a tombstone carrying the local identifier, retirement reason code, actor reference and an RFC 3339 retirement timestamp with seconds and offset, while assertion content is redacted or removed according to the record's retention class.

The retention class, minimum retention period and disposition schedule for control assertions, applicability statements, binding manifests and effectiveness conclusions are set by the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy and by the applicable regulatory regime; this model records the assigned retention class and disposition due date but neither decides nor executes the schedule.

Deletion or disposition of referenced evidence objects, test results, audit records, remediation items, policy documents and catalogue entries is owned and executed by those models; this model deletes only its own reference, digest and assertion records, and marks any dependent conclusion as unsupported rather than silently retaining it as effective.

Erasure requests affecting personal data inside operator, assessor or approver references are executed by the party and identity model; this model replaces the reference with a non-identifying role token, preserves the tombstone and records the erasure event reference.
Purge of a tombstone itself is permitted only under an explicit, logged legal or regulatory instruction recorded by the adopting Dimension's retention authority, never as a routine operation.

roles.name: Control assertion steward
responsibilities: Maintain catalogue bindings and revision pins, and re-assert dependent statuses when a pin changes
Maintain applicability determinations, covered populations and classification values
Keep controlled vocabulary references current and drive migrations when a vocabulary version changes

roles.name: Control owner
responsibilities: Accountable for the design adequacy and continued operation of the control for the host subject
Approve implementation assertions, deviations, exceptions and compensating control declarations
Confirm operator references, operating cadence and trigger declarations

roles.name: Independent assessor
responsibilities: Record assessment method, depth, coverage, sample basis, timing and assessor reference
Bind evidence references with digests and record the sufficiency rationale
Record the effectiveness conclusion and its confidence without operating the control under assessment

roles.name: Risk owner
responsibilities: Accept, suspend or reject a residual contribution attribution claimed by this model
Own the residual value, appetite thresholds and acceptance decision in the risk model
Confirm that each risk-to-control link reflects an intended risk response

roles.name: Model custodian and Dimension registrar
responsibilities: Own the namespace, vocabulary registry, schema versioning and the patch and compatibility rules
Approve composition links to neighbouring models and police boundary creep at review
Assign retention classes and record the policy that owns disposition execution

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Read is granted per host subject to parties holding a declared role in that subject's assertion set; write is granted only to the role that owns the specific record type, and no role may both operate a control and approve its effectiveness conclusion.
exceptions: Independent assessors receive read access across all findings for host subjects within their assessment scope, and write access limited to assessment and evidence bindings and effectiveness conclusions.
Regulators, external auditors and certification bodies receive time-boxed read access to effectiveness conclusions and their basis manifests, recorded as a named disclosure with an expiry timestamp.
Aggregate coverage and effectiveness statistics may be released at bundle scope without per-control detail where the underlying control detail is security-sensitive.
Break-glass read of a control assertion set is permitted during incident response with mandatory post-hoc justification recorded within a defined window.
Risk owners receive read access to linkage, conclusion and residual contribution records for their own risks regardless of subject-level grants.
audit_requirements: Every write, and every read at artifact scope, records actor, role, scope, purpose and a timestamp in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset.

Access and change events are emitted to the audit model, which owns their retention, immutability and trail semantics; this model retains only the emission reference and never asserts trail integrity itself.
Grants of external assessor, regulator or break-glass access are recorded with an expiry timestamp and are reviewed at expiry by the model custodian.
Any read that returns an expired effectiveness conclusion or an unverified binding is logged with the reason so downstream reliance can be traced.

read_order: AGENTS.md for identity, type and the location of every other contract
Specification URL for scope, in-scope and out-of-scope lists and boundary notes against neighbouring models
Storage type URL for the canonical record graph and the rules that govern the chosen projection
Interface URL for read, create, update and delete operations, access scopes and the default deny rule
Processes URL for the linking, applicability, implementation, evidence binding, effectiveness and residual contribution functions and their preconditions
Vocabulary registry URL for the controlled values of every coded field before writing any assertion
Known relations URL to confirm which concepts are owned by target models and must not be modelled locally

coverage.claim: This structure covers the control-linkage, implementation and effectiveness surface of WM-XCT-027 to the depth supported by the cited primary sources, and stops deliberately at references for catalogue, policy, configuration, test, evidence, remediation and audit content owned by neighbouring models. It is not a claim of universal or complete coverage of internal control as a discipline.

checklist.notes: Catalogue binding pins one control reference with source and revision; artifact identity priority names the authoritative master-system identifier first, then governed IRI, then UUID or ULID, and explicitly excludes dates, titles, status values and framework codes.

Design, implementation, operating and effectiveness states are separate, append-only and superseded rather than overwritten; conclusions carry validity windows and invalidation triggers; link retirement and exception expiry are modelled. Remediation and catalogue lifecycles are explicitly external.

Directed risk-to-control links with claimed mechanism, many-to-many coverage topology, control dependency and reliance edges, and framework crosswalks with relation strength. Fifteen composition links record which neighbour owns each adjacent concept.

Event time and observation or ingestion time are separate mandatory fields; assessment timing, covered operating period, applicability window, exception expiry, conclusion validity and attribution effective time are all RFC 3339 with seconds and offset. Interim testing and rollforward are addressed.

Every assertion carries asserting party, event time, observation time, basis reference and reason code on supersession; crosswalks carry author and target version; evidence carries a digest asserted by the owning model at binding time.

Owner, operator, assessor and approver are role-scoped references with independence flags and provided, inherited and customer responsibility splits; five service-layer roles allocate write authority per record type.

Coverage gap detection, crosswalk revalidation on version change, digest verification, evidence sufficiency proportional to control risk, rollforward support, and fail-closed handling of unknown coded values.

Deny by default with bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes; separation of duty between operating and approving; time-boxed regulator and assessor exceptions; break-glass with post-hoc justification.

Tombstone-first retirement with retention class and disposition due date recorded here, while the schedule is owned by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the applicable regime, and disposition of referenced evidence, tests, audit and remediation records is executed by those models.

Format-neutral canonical record graph with round-trip requirement; alignment to the NIST SP 800-53 catalogue and OSCAL implementation and assessment layers, to COSO and GAO internal-control criteria, and to CSF 2.0 and NCSC CAF outcome vocabularies, all as alignment and never conformance.

Functional type, execution mode, operating level and key designation are recorded as source-qualified coded values with a mandatory vocabulary reference, so competing external taxonomies can coexist without being silently merged.

The most widely used published attribute vocabulary for preventive, detective and corrective control type is ISO/IEC 27002:2022, which could not be retrieved (iso.org returned HTTP 403 to every request). The distinction is anchored instead on the GAO Green Book and PCAOB material, and the canonical vocabulary is left Dimension-declared rather than presented as standardised.

Design precision or threshold, expected and observed occurrence counts, sample basis, and attributed reduction with an explicit scale and method are all modelled, each separated from the conclusion they inform.

No consulted primary source prescribes a method for quantifying how much of an inherent-to-residual delta is attributable to one control. The model therefore records the attribution method, its scale and an acceptance status by the risk owner, and does not define or endorse a computation.

Assessment method from examine, interview and test, depth and coverage, assessor independence, evidence references with digests, sufficiency rationale tied to control risk, and a hard rule that a conclusion may cite only verified bindings.

Approved exceptions with expiry, deviations from design, and compensating or alternative controls carrying a sense code that distinguishes the baseline-alternative meaning from the deficiency-mitigating meaning, plus the documented constraint that justifies them.

checklist.dimension: security and confidentiality of control detail
checklist.notes: Access defaults to deny, aggregate statistics can be released without per-control detail where that detail is sensitive, and external disclosure is time-boxed and named.
Physical location enters only as a covered-population or component reference resolved in the host subject or asset model; this mixin holds no geometry and defines no spatial semantics of its own.
